subject: Aurora: SLO spike after quant profile change - p99 latency & error rate
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@aurorafin.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Noticeable latency and 502s since Jan 18 deployment

Hi Rachel,

We started seeing p99 latency jump from ~230ms to ~1.2s and intermittent 502 errors on our production inference calls after the model update you pushed on Jan 18. This spike correlates with the time your team said a new quantization profile was rolled out for the default model.

Our monitoring shows the errors concentrated around longer-context requests (seq >= 1024) and for embeddings calls we saw elevated CPU usage on our side. This is impacting several user flows in our product — two payments-related features have been slowed.

We need an urgent plan: can you confirm whether you rolled a new quant profile for the model serving our account, and whether there is a known performance/compatibility issue? Our SRE is standing by; this is already an active incident for Aurora.

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Sr. Platform Engineer
Aurora Financial

Subject: Re: Fwd: Noticeable latency and 502s since Jan 18 deployment

Rachel / team,

Investigating — preliminary findings below. I pulled logs and a perf dump from the serving hosts handling Aurora traffic (see attached perf_dump_20260119.json).

What I see:
- On Jan 18 at 02:10 UTC we promoted quant profile v2.3 for the catalog model 'redwood-llm-open-7b' for the 'balanced' preset. The profile changes a few kernel selectors and enables an int8 fallback for some attention kernels.
- For long sequences (>=1024) the int8 path is triggering an extra dequantization kernel that currently executes on the CPU in our runtime for some hardware configs. That extra step increases per-token latency substantially for long-context requests, and in saturation scenarios it pushes the worker into a degraded state that returns 502s.
- The failure is more pronounced on the customer's heavy-agent workload which frequently uses seq=2048.

Immediate mitigation options I can implement now:
1) Canary revert: roll back the quant profile to v2.2 for just Aurora's routing policy — should restore previous latency curve within 10-15 minutes if no other dependencies.
2) Hotfix: switch the runtime kernel mapping to prefer GPU dequantization code path; needs a short build and deploy (30-60 minutes) and risk testing.
3) Throttle/route: route Aurora traffic to a fallback model variant (unquantized or previous checkpoint) while we validate. This avoids touching global profile.

I can run option 1 immediately after approval and coordinate with Ops. Attaching the perf dump and a small patch with the diff of profile selectors (quant_profile_diff.patch).

- Dev
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
dev_patel@redwood.ai

Attachments: perf_dump_20260119.json, quant_profile_diff.patch

Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Action plan: rollback applied and interim mitigations (Aurora)

Alex / Lisa — following up with an action update and next steps.

What we did:
- At 16:25 PST on Jan 20 we applied a per-account rollback for Aurora from quant profile v2.3 -> v2.2. Dev confirmed the rollback completed and validated the worker metrics.
- Initial telemetry shows p99 latency dropped from ~1.2s to ~240ms and 502s rate returned to baseline within two verification cycles.

Next steps and timeline:
- Short-term (24–48h): Ops will keep Aurora on v2.2 routing. We will run a focused perf test across seq=512/1024/2048 on a staging shard matching Aurora's hardware to reproduce and gather traces.
- Medium-term (1–2 weeks): Engineering to produce an RCA and a plan to reintroduce a safe quant profile with deterministic GPU dequantization for long sequences or appropriate guards.
- Customer relief: we will issue a usage credit for the 4 hours of degraded service during the incident window (finance approved).

If you notice anything else, reply and we will pick it up immediately. Thank you for your patience — we take SLO regressions seriously and will share a detailed RCA when ready.

Best,
